Looping you both in — customer (Triumph Health) reported a migration-caused duplicate connector that inflated March charges to $18,450.

Quick facts:
- Invoice: MPI-2027-03 (attached by customer)
- Observed spike vs. baseline: ~$16.3k incremental
- Customer asks: invoice correction / goodwill adjustment + VAT guidance

My proposed path:
1) Offer a goodwill settlement to avoid churn given this was an operational migration error.
2) Apply a provisional credit now (so collections are paused) and reissue a corrected invoice once we receive tax residency / VAT evidence.
3) If tax residency proves they are non-EU, reissue net invoice; if EU reverse-charge applies, we reissue accordingly.

Estimated goodwill range: $5k–$8k (to be approved). I'm attaching a quick worksheet with suggested ledger lines and the customer-facing settlement letter draft.

Proposed settlement (summary):
- One-time goodwill settlement: $6,500 credit applied to MPI-2027-03.

- Collections: we will place MPI-2027-03 on hold while this is being resolved.

2) Confirmation whether reverse-charge applies (if billing EU entity).
3) Signature on the settlement letter (DocuSign link below).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/embedded/abcdef123456 (one-click acceptance for Triumph Finance)
